issues.description: Loop invariant for flattenRef is no longer statable in one sentence after the rewrite.
issues.detail: The procedure now mixes three concerns: ref-inheritance, parent-chain refinement subtraction, and $ref propagation when parent was extracted. Each branch mutates `schema` in place and relies on subtle ordering (seen.ref=null guard set before recursive calls). State the invariant explicitly in a literate comment: 'after flattenRef(s), s.schema contains s's own properties plus inherited non-duplicated properties from its ref/parent chain, and seen.ref is null.'

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as structural equality is asymptotically and practically wrong.
issues.detail: Two nested loops `for (const key in schema)` each call `JSON.stringify(schema[key])` and `JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. For a schema with n properties whose values are objects of size m, this is O(n*m) per node and O(N*n*m) overall, with key-order sensitivity producing false negatives (same object, different insertion order, not deduped). Use a structural deep-equal helper, or better, deduplicate by identity when possible.

issues.description: Termination of flattenRef relies on a single seen.ref=null sentinel that is reused for two distinct recursions.
issues.detail: flattenRef recurses on `seen.ref` and also on `seen.parent` (line ~420). Only `seen.ref` is nulled as the recursion guard; the parent recursion has no independent guard. If `parent` forms any chain that re-enters via another node's `parent` link, termination is not obvious. Document why parent chains are guaranteed acyclic, or add an explicit visited set.

issues.description: Override callback semantics changed silently: overrideCount doubled from 6 to 12.
issues.detail: Previously `if (!seen.isParent) override(...)` suppressed overrides on parent nodes; now overrides run for every seen entry. The test was updated to 12 without an explanatory comment. This is a behavior change for any user who registered an `override` callback expecting one call per logical schema. Either restore the guard, or document the new contract in code and changelog.

issues.description: play.ts is repointed at a local source path and left in the diff as a scratch file.
issues.detail: `import * as z from "./packages/zod/src/index.js"` plus console.log debug cases are author scratch, not artifact. This kind of file is exactly what literate programming would extract into a proper example or test. Either delete from the PR or convert the two cases into named tests under `tests/`.

issues.description: Magic `parent: true` flag in ZodType/ZodMiniType `.check` deserves a literate comment.
issues.detail: Both classic and mini now pass `{ parent: true }` to `core.clone`, with the mini change being an uncomment of a previously-disabled flag. A reader cannot tell from the call site what enabling parent linkage means for downstream JSON Schema processing. Add a one-line comment pointing at the parent-chain handling in to-json-schema.ts.

review.summary: The change correctly separates two notions previously conflated in `Seen` — `ref` (processor-supplied inheritance source) and `parent` (clone-chain ancestor) — and that separation is the right data-structure refinement. However, the resulting `flattenRef` procedure is UNDER-AUDITED: no loop/recursion invariant is stated, termination relies on a single nullification sentinel reused across two recursions, and structural equality is implemented by `JSON.stringify` which is both ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW and semantically fragile to key ordering. The override-count test jumping from 6 to 12 reflects a real behavior change in the override contract that should be either reverted or documented. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — the algorithm is plausibly correct but the explanation a future maintainer needs is missing.
